claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK

  - Someone who lives with the child is already claiming
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by getting the first question in the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to know about your child or children. 

**How old is your child (or children)?** Please tell me:
- Their name(s)
- Their age(s) or date(s) of birth

This will help me determine which eligibility requirements apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you have **Alex, who is 8 years old**. Since Alex is under 16, let me move forward with the eligibility check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Alex is under 16, so the first requirement is automatically met. Now let me check the next requirement:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in paid work at all?**

Since Alex is 8 years old, I assume he's not in paid work, so this should be straightforward - but I need to confirm: **Is Alex currently in any paid work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's only 8, so he's just in school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's what I expected. Alex is not in paid work, so that requirement is met. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now the next question:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?** Specifically, is Alex not receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit

Since Alex is 8 and in school, I assume he's not receiving these benefits - but I need to confirm: **Is Alex receiving either of these benefits?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits himself - he's just a child.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That makes sense. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good progress! Now let me check the apprenticeship status:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Given that Alex is only 8 years old and in primary school, I assume he's not in an apprenticeship of any kind. But I need to confirm: **Is Alex currently in any form of apprenticeship?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - he's only 8! He's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! That's clear - Alex is not in any apprenticeship. Let me move forward to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your residency status. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Do you normally live in the UK?** Or do you fall into any of these other categories:

1. **Normally lives in the UK** - You spend most of your time living in the UK
2. **Settled status** - You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. **Pre-settled status and working** - You have pre-settled status and are working (earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months)
4. **Pre-settled status and seeking work** - You have pre-settled status and are actively looking for work
5. **Pre-settled status with sufficient resources** - You have pre-settled status and can financially support yourself and your family without claiming Income Support, income-based JSA, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit
6. **Pre-settled status and studying** - You have pre-settled status, are studying, and have sufficient resources to support yourself
7. **Pre-settled status as a family member** - You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA or Swiss national
8. **Crown servant abroad** - You're living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

**Which of these applies to your situation?** (Or if you normally live in the UK, just let me know that!)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK - I live in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You normally live in the UK, so you meet the residency requirement. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check if you're responsible for Alex. This means:

**Do you live with Alex AND/OR are you contributing to their upkeep?**

Since you're claiming Child Benefit for Alex, I assume you live with him and are responsible for his care. But let me confirm:

1. **Do you live with Alex?**
2. **Are you the main person responsible for Alex's day-to-day care and upkeep** (providing food, clothes, housing, etc.)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, actually Alex doesn't live with me. He lives with his mum.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. Thank you for clarifying that. So Alex lives with his mum, not with you. 

Let me ask a follow-up question to understand your financial involvement:

**Even though Alex doesn't live with you, do you contribute to Alex's upkeep?** For example, do you:
- Pay towards his food, clothes, or other care costs?
- Give him pocket money or presents?
- Contribute towards his housing costs?
- Make maintenance payments under a court order or agreement?

Or are you not providing any financial support towards Alex's care?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not currently contributing anything financially towards Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Unfortunately, based on the eligibility rules, if you don't live with Alex and you're not contributing to his upkeep, you don't meet the responsibility requirement for Child Benefit.

Let me navigate to the outcome to confirm this:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the eligibility assessment, here's the outcome:

---

## **INELIGIBLE for Child Benefit**

**Reason:** You are not responsible for Alex

**Explanation:**

To be eligible for Child Benefit, you must be responsible for the child. This means you must either:
1. **Live with the child**, OR
2. **Contribute to the child's upkeep** by paying at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards their care (including food, clothes, housing, pocket money, etc.)

This can also include maintenance payments under a court order or agreement.

Since Alex lives with his mum and you're not currently contributing financially towards his care, you don't meet the responsibility requirement.

---

**Next Steps:**

If your situation changes and you start to contribute financially towards Alex's upkeep (for example, through a child maintenance agreement), or if you become the main carer and Alex comes to live with you, you may become eligible. In that case, you could reapply.

Alternatively, **Alex's mum** may be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him, as she is the one living with and caring for him.

If you have any questions about this decision or need further support, you can contact HMRC's Child Benefit team on **0300 200 3100**.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. So because Alex doesn't live with me and I'm not paying towards his care, I can't claim Child Benefit for him. That makes sense - his mum would be the one who could claim it then since she's the one looking after him day to day. Thank you for explaining that to me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! Yes, exactly right - you've understood it perfectly. Since Alex's mum is the one living with him and caring for him day-to-day, she would be the appropriate person to claim Child Benefit for him.

If Alex's mum would like to check her own eligibility for Child Benefit, she can:
- Go through an assessment like this one
- Visit **www.gov.uk/child-benefit** for more information
- Contact HMRC on **0300 200 3100** if she has any questions

Thank you for using this service, and I hope this has helped clarify things. If you have any other questions in the future, feel free to ask!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Thank you, that's been really helpful. I'll let her know she should look into claiming it. Have a good day!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! That's great - I'm glad I could help clarify things for you. Yes, do let Alex's mum know to look into it, as she'll likely be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Have a great day, and thanks for using this service! 👋

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: You're welcome! Thanks again, bye!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Bye! Take care! 👋

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
*conversation ends naturally*

---

**Out of character note for evaluation purposes:**

The eligibility agent correctly determined that the claimant is **INELIGIBLE** for Child Benefit because:
1. The child (Alex) does not live with the claimant
2. The claimant does not contribute financially to the child's upkeep

This matches the situation profile where Alex "does not live with you" and there was no indication of financial contributions. The agent appropriately identified that the child's mother (who Alex lives with) would be the eligible claimant instead.

The conversation flowed naturally and the agent asked appropriate follow-up questions to establish both living arrangements and financial responsibility before reaching the correct conclusion.
